title: Escalation Velocity Handbook and Game Day Lab Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This handbook defines a compact, measurable escalation velocity model for LLM-serving incidents and provides an accompanying game-day lab bundle for training and validating responder teams. The goal is to shorten time-to-stabilize while preserving forensic quality and consistent customer communications.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood inference production services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane).
- Focus on incidents with customer-impacting latency, error-rate, or model-quality regressions.
- Includes on-call workflow, escalation thresholds, evidence checklist, and a reusable game-day exercise.

Key definitions:
- Escalation Velocity: time from first alert to escalation to the next responder tier. Target: P1 < 10 minutes, P2 < 30 minutes.
- Stabilize: service returns to SLO baseline for 30 minutes (rolling).
- Evidence Packet: minimal set of artifacts to attach to an incident for regulatory/enterprise requests.

Roles & Responsibilities:
1. First Responder (FR): owns initial triage, immediate mitigations, and evidence collection.
2. Bridge Conductor (BC): runs the incident bridge, coordinates stakeholders and external comms.
3. Service Steward: long-term owner for restoration and root cause analysis.
4. Escalation Triage Team (ETT): cross-functional engineers for multi-service or model regressions.

Escalation Velocity Matrix (table):
- Severity | Primary Signal | Target Velocity | Initial Action
- P0 (emergency) | Total region outage or pipeline failure | 0-5 min | Pager + channel + full bridge
- P1 (critical) | >5% 5m error-rate or 99th percentile latency breach >2x SLO | 0-10 min | Pager to FR, immediate throttling/fallback
- P2 (high) | 1-5% error-rate or sustained SLO drift | 10-30 min | Alert to primary on-call, begin scoped mitigation
- P3 (medium) | transient warnings or increased tail-latency <3x SLO | 1-8 hours | Ticket, monitor, schedule fix

Triage Decision Ladder (step-by-step):
1. Acknowledge (0-2m): FR confirms alert and posts to #incidents with severity and first observations.
2. Scope (2-8m): Identify impacted regions, models, customers, and whether degradation is progressive or abrupt.
3. Contain (2-15m): Apply safe mitigations: route to standby model, enable KV cache bypass, reduce batch size, throttle low-tier traffic.
4. Escalate (if not stabilized within target velocity): call ETT and Bridge Conductor.
5. Stabilize & Record (until SLO baseline maintained for 30m): collect evidence packet and update status page.

Rapid Mitigation Playbook (common actions):
- Latency spike: temporarily reduce batching window to 20ms, switch to lower-seqlen model variant, enable per-tenant rate caps.
- Error surge: switch traffic to last-known-good model snapshot, toggle per-route fallback, mark feature flags.
- KV cache thrash: clear and warm cache selectively (avoid cluster-wide flush), increase cache TTL for hot prefixes.

Bridge Conductor Checklist (first 10 minutes):
- Create bridge and invite FR, BC, Service Steward, ETT, and CS lead.
- Post incident summary template to bridge: severity, observed start, primary signal, tentative impact.
- Assign communications owner and legal/comm liaison if enterprise customers are affected.
- Document mitigation actions and immediate next steps in the bridge notes.

Evidence Packet (mandatory artifacts):
- Incident timeline (timestamps, actor, action)
- Alert payloads and metric graphs (5m, 1h, 6h windows)
- Representative request/response traces including token counts and latencies (anonymize PII)
- Model version and config snapshot (quantization, batching, kernel selection)
- Any infra-level adjustments (scales, instance restarts, kernel toggles)
- Status page updates and customer messages with timestamps
Retention: keep packet for 90 days for internal RCA, 365 days for enterprise evidence when requested.

Customer Communication Templates (staged):
- Initial status (public): "We are investigating increased latency for the Redwood API in region X. Engineers are on the issue and we will provide updates every 15 minutes."
- Operational update: "Reduction in error-rate observed after routing changes. We are monitoring; no customer action required at this time."
- Resolution: "Service restored to normal performance at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC. We have opened a post-incident review and will follow up with details within 72 hours if customers request."
- Enterprise notice (sensitive): include incident ID, timeline, affected tenants, mitigations applied, and next steps for remediation and credits.

Postmortem Quick Template (to be completed within 72 hours):
- Title, Severity, Incident ID, Summary (one paragraph)
- Timeline (epoched events)
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence
- Corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and due dates
- Customer impact and comms log
- Follow-up evals: model-quality checks, regression suites to add, and game-day re-run plan

Game Day Lab (exercise & scoring):
- Goal: validate escalation velocity, evidence collection fidelity, and customer comms cadence.
- Duration: 90 minutes including debrief.
- Roles required: FR, BC, ETT (2+), CS observer, Legal observer.
- Scenario examples: simulated KV cache thrash on regional Dedicated pool; abrupt model rollout causing high-latency tails; multi-tenant noisy neighbor saturation.
- Scoring rubric (pass/fail thresholds):
  - Acknowledge & bridge creation <= 5m (pass)
  - Evidence packet complete by end of exercise (pass)
  - Customer initial status posted <= 10m (pass)
  - Escalation velocity targets met for severity (P1<=10m) (pass/fail)

Handoff Protocol (end-of-shift checklist):
- FR prepares a 15-minute HAT (Handoff and Triage) note in the bridge with: current state, known unknowns, outstanding actions, and next steps.
- On-call receiving: replicate smoke checks (latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate), validate ticket assignment, confirm acceptance in channel.

Runbook Ownership & Maintenance:
- Each runbook has an owner and a quarterly review stamp. Owners must run a short tabletop or synthetic test annually.
- Deprecated runbooks are archived with clear deprecation date in the header.

Appendix: CLI snippets & runbook links:
- Gather traces: 
  curl -sS "$METRICS_URL/api/trace?start=now-15m&service=inference" > traces.json
- Snapshot model config: 
  rcli model snapshot --service inference --model-id $MODEL --out model-snapshot.json

Related pages & templates:
- Use this document as the canonical escalation-velocity spec and attach the Game Day Lab template (exercise-template.md) to new hire on-call bootcamps.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-02: Initial publish by Aisha Patel.
- 2026-02-15: Updated evidence packet retention and added game-day scoring rubric.
